questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I choose on behalf of my interest for economics. Normally i study molecular biomedicin. but i have an interest in mathematics and economics. This interest got satisfied when i applied for a semester at GSEM.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall great, but i got to experience alot of set backs along the way. UNIGE made it pretty difficult to know what was expected of the person prior to starting the course. Please be aware of that when applying. Additionally th workload was extremey high if attending GSEM compared to UNIGE law. This was quiet unexpected and set some boundaries for, what was possible to do during a weekend - as you had to study. The criterias to past was extremely high. you need to get 70% correct to pass a class, which is quiet different from the danish system.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The university provided me with all the neccesary information upon arrival. So no stress was found.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university provided guided tours on campus upon arrival. Additionally did they provide course information as well of all general information regarding all you needed to know.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in a 1 bedroom studio appartment. This was the main accomodation providement. But it was possible to applie for a shared appartment as well.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: None. But you could buy a meal at the university once a day at cheap prices.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: All accomodation is expensive in geneva, but choosing on campus accomodation is convenient due to the short travel distance to the faculties. Be aware of the deadline dates. Applying for UNIGE in the second round, will make it difficult to apply for housing because many deadlines is already past at that point.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They tell you to access your university course site and apply for the courses. This is shown to you in the class - how to do it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The teachers helped you with the details for applying to a course.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all the classes i applied for. But be aware of the course descriptions. If they suggest that you should have done a course in advance to the following course, you should have done it. I applied for two classes, where I figure out halfway through the course that i needed to have done a course prior to that. I did those, but that ment that i needed to do 12 ECTS of self studying. So if they suggest a course, this is mandatory and not a good idea. They expect you to have passed that course and know everything from that course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advise future exchange students to start the registration process early and carefully follow the instructions provided by the University of Geneva. Some administrative steps, such as course enrollment and obtaining a student ID, may take time, so it’s important to stay organized and check deadlines. Additionally, contacting the international office for any uncertainties can help avoid delays.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was very high. Some courses were particularly challenging due to the lack of technological support during exams. No technological assisting devices were provided, which made certain subjects more demanding. I would recommend future students to be aware of this and prepare accordingly when starting their courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At my home university, I typically read extensively in advance, with classes serving as support for my learning. At the host university, it was presented as if attending lectures alone would be sufficient to pass, but this was not the case. This approach allowed them to allocate more lectures within the given ECTS, which meant that additional self-study was still necessary to fully grasp the material. I therefore studied for around 70-80 hours a weak in mean. They give you a "self study sylabus", which is highly needed to study - if you want to pass the class.
